package_info.package_versions: Not specified (all versions with vulnerable report_admin.php and host.php code)
package_info.why_malicious: The application is vulnerable because it fails to properly escape user-supplied input (device name) before rendering it in the admin reporting interface, allowing stored JavaScript payloads to execute in the browser of privileged users (Stored XSS).

required_permissions: filesystem (write to DB via web interface)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code concatenates the $title and $description variables (populated from user-controlled database fields) and outputs them directly into the HTML response without escaping, allowing stored JavaScript payloads to execute in the victim's browser.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Directly outputting user-controlled data into HTML without escaping enables attackers to inject and execute arbitrary JavaScript in the context of the victim's session.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior would escape or sanitize all user-supplied data before rendering it in the browser to prevent XSS. Here, the application fails to do so.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Concatenating and displaying database fields is common, but only when proper output encoding is applied.
key_indicators: Lack of output escaping or sanitization
Direct concatenation of user-controlled variables into HTML
Rendering of device name/description fields in admin interface

execution_context.trigger: user input (device name set via host.php), then runtime (when admin views reports_admin.php)
execution_context.file_location: host.php (device name input form, stored in DB)
required_permissions: web application access (authenticated user with Sites/Devices/Data permissions)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At input time, an attacker supplies a malicious device name containing a script tag. When an admin later views the reports_admin.php page, the payload is rendered and executed in the browser, resulting in stored XSS.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Device names should be treated as plain text, not executable code. Allowing HTML/JS in this field is a clear XSS vector.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal device name input should be sanitized and encoded before storage and output. Here, arbitrary HTML/JS is accepted and rendered.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; device names should never contain executable code.
key_indicators: Presence of <script> tags in user-supplied input
Lack of input validation or output encoding
Execution of user-supplied JS in admin context

attack_chain.action: Attacker with authenticated access submits a device name containing a malicious JavaScript payload via host.php.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious payload is stored in the database.

attack_chain.action: Admin user visits reports_admin.php, which retrieves and renders the device name/description fields without escaping.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious JavaScript executes in the admin's browser (stored XSS).

attack_chain.action: Malicious JavaScript executes in the context of the admin session, enabling account takeover, data theft, or further attacks.
attack_chain.leads_to: Final goal: compromise of admin account or further exploitation.

behavioral_signatures: User-supplied input rendered in HTML without escaping
Presence of <script> or other HTML tags in device name/description fields
Execution of JavaScript in admin interface sourced from database fields
file_indicators: host.php (device name input form without validation)
network_indicators: Unusual HTTP requests to /cacti/host.php with device names containing HTML/JS
Subsequent GET requests to /cacti/reports_admin.php resulting in script execution
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for user-supplied input fields (such as device name) that are rendered in HTML responses without proper escaping or sanitization. Scan database fields for suspicious patterns like <script> tags. Use web application firewalls (WAF) to detect and block requests containing potential XSS payloads. Review source code for direct output of user-controlled variables into HTML. Monitor browser console logs for unexpected script execution in admin interfaces.
